definition: Made by professionals or organizations for people to use about their own or their family's health.
example: A CDC page on how much sleep teens need.
notes: Most health content. Pair with level-1 and level-2 audiences.

definition: Made for people to use in their work: to practise, teach, run a program or pass information on. A very large category; the narrower concepts say what the professional does with it.
notes: The audience roles (clinicians, health communicators, school and campus leaders...) say which professional and therefore which level. Kalman, 22 Oct: a lot of communications fall into this category.

definition: Tells professionals what to do in their own practice.
example: ACSM guidelines for prescribing exercise; AASM sleep duration recommendations.
notes: SleepLiteracy example: ACSM 'Guidelines for prescribing exercise in medicine'.

definition: Made for professionals to hand on, present or adapt for the people they serve. Two audiences: the professional who uses it and the public who ends up reading it.
example: World Sleep Day toolkit with editable slides; patient fact sheets for clinicians to give out.
mesh: D029282 Patient Education Handout|D033181 Information Dissemination
notes: Tag both directions' audiences, e.g. clinicians + the person themselves. MeSH Patient Education Handout is a publication type. SleepLiteracy examples: World Sleep Day resources; Sleep Health Foundation fact sheets.

definition: Teaches professionals new skills or knowledge, often for credit.
example: NIOSH's online shift-work and sleep training for nurses.
mesh: D004496 Education, Continuing|D004502 Education, Medical, Continuing

definition: Reports what was studied and found, mainly for other researchers and evidence users.
example: A systematic review of school start times and teen sleep.
notes: Most journal articles. The sleep-research note shows these tag populations, not actors.

alt_labels: implementation guides|program manuals|policy templates|how-to for organizations
definition: Helps professionals set up a program or change how their organization works.
example: A guide for campuses on moving early exams.
notes: Pairs with level-3 and level-4 audiences.

definition: Made to inform or persuade people who decide policy.
example: A brief for state legislators on school start times.
notes: Pairs with level-5 audiences and the proposed advocacy-phase facet (research/advocacy-frameworks).

definition: Made by members of the public for each other, from lived experience.
example: A narcolepsy support community's tips for college.

definition: People and communities telling professionals and decision-makers what they need.
example: A survey of shift workers' sleep needs shared with employers.
notes: Rarely tagged anywhere; useful for participatory and policy work.
